page.layout: One column of running text, full width; below the last line, right-aligned, the catchword "EPIST."; running head at the top, centred over the text; page number at the head, left. No marginal notes.

main_text.p: quamquam characteres eosdem esse facile judicarem, in omnibus tamen fere dissimilitudinem aliquam deprehendi, sed multo majorem in libello quodam Romae recens Italice excuso, quem ante paucos dies raptim legi. Sed literam Tau de qua in opusculo tuo docte disputas, hac semper forma [illegible, ~1 letters] in eo Codice effictam video, quae parum ad crueem mihi pertinere videtur. Unum vir doctissime, te plurimum rogatum velim, idmodo tibi non sit oneri futurum, ut cum otio abundabis, inscriptiones Siclorum, de quibus mentionem facis, iisdem, quibus scripti sunt, characteribus exscribicures, & ad me mittere non graveris: editionem Pentateuchi Samaritani jussu Illustrissimi Cardinalis Berulli meditor; inscriptiones ejusmodi coeptum meum plurimum adjuvabunt: Preces meae parum civiles, ne temerarias dicam, videri possunt, qui adeo repetita amicitia tua abutar; sed eas ut spero, facile excusabunt & tuum in litteras studium, & tua in me humanitas.

page.notes: The letter after "forma" is a Samaritan letter (Tau, as the text discusses) that I cannot reproduce reliably, so it is marked illegible. "crueem" is printed for "crucem" (a printer's error, left as printed). "exscribi" ends a line with no printed hyphen before "cures"; written as "exscribicures" per the rule, though the printer may have omitted a hyphen. "dif-" at the line end before "fimilitudinem" is read as "dis-" (long s), giving "dissimilitudinem". The catchword "EPIST." is right-aligned below the text.
